claim_reviews.rationale: Jones §1 describes chiefly bronze fragments and gearwork; Anastasiou §1 documents the device and spirals. Greek and craftsmanship are supported at this level.
The changed attribution correctly characterizes Freeth’s stated construction estimate, not a firm date; Jones §1 discusses substantially broader limits. Other clauses unchanged from baseline.

Jones §1 says letter forms permit about 225 BCE to just before the wreck and estimates the wreck at 60 ± 10 BCE from coins and pottery. The revised approximate range uses the later end of that probable wreck estimate, explicitly discloses this derivation, and does not present it as a certain hard cutoff. Freeth’s late-second-century construction estimate remains attributed in the event. Jones also notes dates over 20 years from 60 BCE are rather unlikely, not impossible; the range remains approximate.

Freeth estimates end second century; Jones dates are uncertain. Anastasiou §1 and Jones §2 identify 235 lunar months, 19 years, five turns, Fragment B and the inscription. Anastasiou §§1–2.2 identifies preserved pointer and pin, reconstructs sliding hub, and reports last gear missing. Iversen/Jones §1 identifies the 223-month eclipse scale and one-third survival. Reconstruction is attributed and not confused with observed intact mounting.
New citations and locators identify relevant original arguments and differentiate missing gear, reconstruction and physical fragments; source metadata and saved evidence checksum match.

Date question follows Jones §1 on insecure paleographic comparanda and difference between epoch and manufacture. Missing-drive question follows Anastasiou §1 and §2.1; this is an explicit question, not an established new connection.

Existing link and endpoint inspected. The 223-month correspondence does not establish direction or route to this particular instrument; remain candidate, not established history. No new consequential relation proposed; independent corroboration of this specific connection is absent.

duplicate_screen.rationale: Baseline existing gearing record has the same artifact and archaeological event. Metonic calendar and pointer add supported detail to that event, not a new record. Search of discovery records for Antikythera and Metonic yielded that record; broad gearing remains distinct from particular display.

unknowns: The specific drive train and final gear remain missing.
No established route from Babylonian astronomy to this particular instrument was demonstrated.
